Made by D. S. Pitts. Forwarded by.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 15 AUG 1939 SHANGHAI）
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 15 AUG 1939 SHANGHAI）

With reference to the contents of the letter
signed by one Ignaz PIVNIK received by Mr. H. E.
OLSEN, Deputy Commissioner of Customs, I have to
report that the writer, a refugee who arrived
here from Europe on May 22, 1939, has been warned
by the International Relief Fund Committee to
refrain from sending any further letters of this
nature, otherwise he will find himself in serious
trouble. PIVNIK, born in Vienna on November 26, 1915,
is registered under No. 5749 with the I. C. Committee.

Ja Giles
D. S.

pages.en:
Mr.
Chief Olsen H. E.

Shanghai, 8. August 1939.

Dear Sir,
I beg to adress these lines to you in the hope that will give
them your kind consideration.
I have recently arrived here as an emigrant from Germany
trusting to find a position in my own trade or some other work. So
far I have not been successful.
Now, my wife, who is still in Germany, has informed me that
she too has to leave Germany very shortly. There exists a difficulty
however, i. e. that payment for ship's passage has to be effected in
foreign currency, because German shipping lines who accept German cur-
rency (R. M.) have already sold out their space as far ahead as till
the beginning of the next year. The point now is to get foreign currency.
Since I have no means myself I am being put before the task of raising
the necessary amount, which by the way is round Sh. 1200.- = £.-/-
somehow, and I am thinking, that by soliciting contributions from some
of my more fortunate fellow-beings in Shanghai I might be able to succeed
in the solving of my task.
The purpose of these lines is to appeal to you for a contribution
I shall be ever grateful to you for even the smallest amount you may see
fit to contribute. I intend keeping a record of all the kind people who,
by their generosity are lending their help to a good cause, and I shall
deem it my first duty to successfully refund the contributions to the
kind donors as soon as I have been able to find work again.
I beg to enclose an envelope herein bearing the address under
which your contribution will reach me, viz.:
Mr. Ignaz Livnik c/o P. O. Box 1131, Shanghai.

Before closing my letter I would like to inform you that I am
a practical expert on all machine-tools, with several years of workshop-
praxis, 34 years of age, and willing to work in any capacity. If you,
Sir, perchance should know or hear of any possible vacancy, I should
feel immensely obliged to you if you would kindly inform me about it,
without any obligation to yourself of course.
Apologizing for having taken your time and expressing in ad-
vance my heartfelt thanks for kind assistance
I am, Dear Sir,
most respectfully yours

(I. Livnik.)
Ignaz Livnik

DC. (S.B).
Send to Mr Olsen Deputy Commr. Customs,
looks like a dacker as he states -
his claim. Any record please!

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER OF CUSTOMS
SHANGHAI
11 AUG 1939）
pages.zh:
致
H. E. Olsen 首席先生

上海，1939年8月8日。

尊敬的先生：
我冒昧致函阁下，恳请惠予垂注。
我最近作为来自德国的移民抵达此地，希望能找到一份本行工作或其它工作。但至今未果。
如今，仍留在德国的妻子告知我，她也必须很快离开德国。然而存在一个困难，即船票费用必须以外币支付，因为接受德国货币（帝国马克）的德国航运公司的舱位已售罄至明年年初。现在的关键是获取外币。
由于我身无分文，我面临着筹集必要资金的任务，这笔金额大约为申洋1200元 = 英镑若干，我在想，通过向上海一些较我幸运的同胞募捐，或许能够成功解决这一难题。
此信的目的是恳请阁下捐款。对于阁下认为适宜捐赠的任何微小金额，我都将感激不尽。我打算记录所有慷慨解囊、助力善举的好心人，并将把尽快偿还好心捐赠者的捐款视为我的首要义务，一旦我重新找到工作，便立即执行。
随信附上一个信封，上面印有接收捐款的地址，即：
Ignaz Livnik 先生 转 上海邮政信箱 1131 号。

在结束此信之前，我想告知阁下，我是一名拥有多年车间实践经验的机床实用专家，现年34岁，愿意从事任何职位的工作。如果阁下碰巧知道或听说有任何可能的空缺，若蒙告知，我将不胜感激，当然这并不强求阁下。
为占用阁下的时间致歉，并预先对阁下的善意援助表示衷心感谢
尊敬的先生，
您最恭敬的仆人

(I. Livnik.)
Ignaz Livnik

副总监（特别分部）。
送交海关副税务司 Olsen 先生，
看起来像他所说的——
一种骗局。请查有无记录！

（印：海关副税务司
上海
1939年8月11日）

CUSTOM HOUSE.
Shanghai , 11th August, 1939.

G. W. Gilbert, Esquire,
Police Head Quarter,
Foochow Road,
S H A N G H A I.

My Dear Gilbert,
I received the unclosed in this
morning mail looks like it may be a "racket",
will you please pass it on to the Department
concerned.
I am confined to bed otherwise
I would have brought it over personally.
Yours,
pages.zh:
海关。
上海，1939年8月11日。

G. W. Gilbert 先生，
警察总局，
福州路，
上 海。

亲爱的 Gilbert：
今晨邮件中收到附件，看起来可能是一种“骗局”，
能否请您将其转交相关部门处理。
我因病卧床，否则我会亲自送来。
此致，
